questions.prompt: What is the capital city of The Gambia?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the The Gambia article.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with The Gambia?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture The Gambia on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the The Gambia article.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of The Gambia?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Culture” part of the The Gambia article.

questions.proof: English is the official language, but people speak other languages as well.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It was ruled by Dawda Jawara and his People's Progressive Party (PPP) from _____ to 1994.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the The Gambia article, under the heading “Politics and government”.

questions.proof: It was ruled by Dawda Jawara and his People's Progressive Party (PPP) from 1965 to 1994.
